label: Critically ill women who died
plain_language: About 1 in 9 women who reached a severe outcome died; the rest were near-misses who survived.
headline: yes

label: Near-misses for every death
plain_language: For every mother who died, nearly eight others came close - a large, learnable warning signal that deaths alone miss.

label: Hospital maternal death rate
plain_language: Among live births at this hospital, the maternal death rate worked out to about 460 per 100,000 - in the range of Tanzania's high national figures.
headline: yes

label: Severe cases from direct causes
plain_language: Three quarters of the life-threatening cases came from direct causes of pregnancy and birth, not other illnesses.

label: Hypertensive disorders (of deaths)
plain_language: High-blood-pressure disorders in pregnancy, including pre-eclampsia and eclampsia, caused a quarter of the deaths.
headline: yes

label: Postpartum haemorrhage (of deaths)
plain_language: Heavy bleeding after birth was among the top killers, and the study calls it the leading cause among these women.

label: Severe anaemia (of deaths)
plain_language: Severe anaemia, an indirect cause, killed as many of these women as the leading direct causes did.

label: Cardiovascular disease (of deaths)
plain_language: Heart and blood-vessel disease was an equally common cause of death, and is easy to overlook.

label: Postpartum haemorrhage (of severe cases)
plain_language: Bleeding after birth was the single most common reason a woman became critically ill.

label: Pregnancies with a poor outcome for the baby
plain_language: Almost half of these pregnancies ended badly for the baby - a stillbirth, an early death, or serious complications at birth.
headline: yes

label: Perinatal deaths among the 140 pregnancies
plain_language: 39 babies were stillborn or died in the first days of life among these 140 high-risk pregnancies.

label: Women given too little blood
plain_language: More than half the women needed a blood transfusion, and about 40% of them received less than physicians prescribed.
